newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks end down as benchmark Telefonica cut.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks end down as benchmark Telefonica cut.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed down Tuesday, dragged lower by Telefonica del Peru after Merrill Lynch & Co cut the telecom's medium-term rating to accumulate from buy, brokers said.

While Merrill Lynch's cut was due to the Lima benchmark's price approaching a ceiling of $30 on its American Depositary Shares in New York, the new rating had a direct impact on local trade in Telefonica, they added.
Tuesday, the General Index IGRA fell 2.51 percent to 2,074.1 points, according to preliminary figures given at the market's close.
The blue-chip Selective Index ISEL dropped 2.88 percent to 2,984.8 points.
In a total of 2,016 trades, volume was a healthy 40.3 million soles ($15.2 million), brokers said.
The market will likely see more falls Wednesday as investors believe shares are overpriced following their strong rises in May, they added.

"The euphoria of previous weeks is over and investors are now saying they only want sure gains. Many shares have reached a ceiling that will apply for the long term," said Efran Chvez of the local brokerage Plusvalor.
Telefnica B shares fell 2.74 percent to 6.74 soles on volume of 936,000 shares.
Peru's largest brewery group Unin de Cerveceras Peruanas Backus y Johnston SA dropped 3.08 percent to 2.52 soles on volume of 2.1 million shares.
The only blue chip to resist the undertow was financial holding company Credicorp, which rose 0.22 percent to $22.45 on volume of 30,200 shares.
